laurel.name: Laurel Mack
laurel.role: Grieving mother frozen ten years after her daughter's vanishing
laurel.look: A slender 55-year-old British woman with sorrowful hazel eyes, tired posture, chin-length faded blonde hair, wearing a neutral knit cardigan and wool trousers in contemporary London.

floyd.name: Floyd Dunn
floyd.role: Charming, self-deprecating mathematics professor harboring dark complicity
floyd.look: A charismatic 56-year-old man with silver-flecked brown hair, gentle smile, scholarly glasses, wearing an unstructured tweed blazer and soft button-down shirt.

noelle.name: Noelle Donnelly
noelle.role: Former math tutor whose obsessive entitlement orchestrated the tragedy
noelle.look: A plain, intense 40-year-old woman with severe dark hair pulled back tightly, sharp calculating gaze, wearing an unadorned wool coat and modest blouse in 2005.

ellie.name: Ellie Mack
ellie.role: The fifteen-year-old golden daughter who vanished on her way to the library
ellie.look: A luminous 15-year-old British schoolgirl with long golden hair, bright green eyes with a cupid's bow smile, wearing a navy school uniform and canvas bag in 2005.

poppy.name: Poppy Dunn
poppy.role: Floyd's nine-year-old prodigy daughter bearing an uncanny resemblance to Ellie
poppy.look: A poised, quiet 9-year-old girl with wavy honey-colored hair, distinctive green eyes, head tilted slightly, wearing a neat woolen pinafore dress in a sunny kitchen.

hannah.name: Hannah Mack
hannah.role: Laurel's surviving elder daughter living in the shadow of her sister's ghost
hannah.look: A guarded 27-year-old woman with dark blonde hair in a messy bun, guarded posture, dressed in practical contemporary jeans and an olive green field jacket.

room.look: A dark subterranean room and basement, stark walls, heavy wooden doors, dim ceiling lamp evoking quiet claustrophobic dread.

library.look: A traditional brick community library with tall arched windows, shelves of books, quiet reading tables under brass lamps.

objects.why: The central theme of shattered domestic bonds and the illusion of safety.
The routine domestic act in the kitchen that triggers Laurel's horrifying recognition.
The missing poster and childhood portraits comparing Ellie and Poppy.
The physical reality of the flower bed and buried truth.
The false sanctuary of domestic life masking captivity and denial.
The cellar threshold and domestic barriers separating reality from illusion.
The uncanny genetic reflection between Ellie and Poppy.
The fragile psychological defenses Laurel constructs to survive unbearable grief.
The charming public personas of Floyd and Noelle concealing dark realities.
The library revision textbooks Ellie carried the afternoon she vanished.

spine.claim: Desperate maternal grief creates an obsessive vacuum that leaves Laurel vulnerable to comforting counterfeit intimacies.
Meeting Floyd and seeing nine-year-old Poppy forces Laurel into an uncanny valley where maternal instinct collides with rational disbelief.
Uncovering Noelle Donnelly's subterranean captivity reveals that monstrous entitlement operated directly beneath ordinary domestic routines.
Floyd's intellectualized denial and complicity expose how passive ignorance sustains unspeakable violence.
True survival requires tearing down comforting illusions and embracing the painful, complex inheritance of love and grief.
